extra.reason: Added DodoRouter.Usage to resolve the convention from the numbers (cache tokens exceeding prompt_tokens => provider reports them separately); wired into log list, router show, log detail, Logs.cache_stats hit_rate, and Models.calculate_cost.

Implemented fresh against current main rather than rebasing any of the three heads — all were 2+ weeks stale and conflicted pairwise. Single policy point in Adapter.build_forwarded_headers/2: forward by default, strip for three stated reasons (replace / provider breaks / not the client's to send). Edge headers by PREFIX (x-forwarded-, cf-) not enumeration. Deviated from kuxnqlvl on openai-beta — it is a feature opt-in like anthropic-beta, not account scope, so it forwards. No DodoRouterWeb.ForwardedHeaders module: the only thing needing conn was the session-header strip, and session headers now forward. Also deleted the hop-by-hop filter that was triplicated across all three proxy controllers.

anthropic-beta now merges instead of colliding: Anthropic.request_headers/2 folds the client's beta list into the proxy's own headers BEFORE the generic proxy-wins rule runs, so exactly one merged header goes upstream with oauth-2025-04-20 guaranteed on sk-ant-oat tokens. call/4 and stream/5 no longer ignore their client_headers argument. count_tokens extended to /4 and threaded through the controller — Claude Code calls it before compaction, and counting against a different beta set than the request that follows answers a question about a request we are not going to send. user-agent and x-app need no special casing; they forward under the default policy.

Verified @consumed_fields is still accurate against the current converters before landing — Anthropic's list matches exactly; Responses' 'reasoning' entry is consumed via pattern match in client_reasoning_effort/1 rather than bracket access, so it is correct despite not appearing in a naive grep. 996 tests, 0 failures; precommit exit 0.

Applied jj lrtztplp; anthropic_format.ex, and both test files took git apply --3way cleanly, anthropic.ex needed context-based apply (offset 45 lines) because dor.5's header edits are uncommitted so there is no index blob to 3-way against. Verified both seams the commit depends on: @allowed_request_fields still carries tool_choice and response_format (so OpenAI-family providers pick them up on fallback as claimed), and @consumed_fields correctly grew by 'tool_choice output_config' so the dor.2 detector does not now report them as dropped. 1017 tests, 0 failures; precommit exit 0.

Won't do — Gezim's call, 2026-08-11. The diff is the product: client headers are already stored, and for the body the panel names what was dropped, which answers 'why didn't my request do X'. Storing a near-duplicate of the IR body at Claude Code sizes costs real storage for marginal value.

Fidelity.record_dropped_body_fields/3 and record_dropped_response_fields/2 now take a name => value map and record the value alongside the name: JSON-encoded, run through Redact.redact_secrets/1, and capped at 2000 chars with a visible '… [truncated, N more characters]' marker. Callers updated: Adapter.sanitize_request (egress allowlist), FallbackChain.apply_passthrough and split_response_passthrough, and the Responses ingress via the new Fidelity.dropped_body_changes/3. Header rows deliberately carry no value (credentials/edge headers), and the silent reasons still record nothing. Rendered on the log detail Trace under 'what you sent', collapsed by default. Tests in fidelity_test.exs and log_live_test.exs.

Resolved by rebuilding the tab strip as a hop timeline. 'Sent to Provider', 'Final Response' and 'Provider Details' are gone; the log detail now has two modes, Conversation (what was said) and Trace (the wire). The Trace renders one node per hop in order — You sent / Attempt N per provider attempt / You received — with each fidelity change on the edge between the hops that produced it, so the old 'Step' column pointing at another tab is unnecessary. Each node expands to its own endpoint, key, outbound headers, request body, outbound body, error body, response body and response headers. Two mislabelings found and fixed while doing it: the top node no longer implies the stored IR is the client's body (it isn't stored, and the node says so), and the final node's body is labelled 'recorded before conversion to <format>' for non-OpenAI clients because the log holds the IR, not the egress bytes. Verified in Chrome against localhost:4000 on clean, dropped-field and two-attempt fallback logs.
